citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
This edge-only validation regression deliberately supplies no node
 contents. Its records assert selection dependencies only. Domain
 requires this callback, but reaching it would introduce an unwanted
 content read and fail this guard.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[agent_edge_tools_record_selections_without_validating_targets]/impl[GraphWithChangingEdges/Domain]/fn[node_content]` is a function-level exception, and the item is an explicit function with a body. Its fenced commentary gives a substantive reason, and the current source agrees with that reason.

- The enclosing test only exercises `outgoing_edges` tool calls, which is the edge-only scenario the commentary describes. Its assertions check `Dependency::OutgoingEdges` records, the tool-result JSON, lookup counts and stored evidence. It never asserts anything about node contents.
- `Domain` requires `node_content`, so the test graph has to define it. The body is `panic!("edge inspection must not read node contents")`. A content read would therefore fail the test, so the callback is meant to stay unexecuted. That matches the commentary's "unwanted content read and fail this guard".
- The test's `Domain` impl defines its own `outgoing_edges`, `load_evidence` and `store_evidence`. These are the items the test actually uses, so nothing in the test needs `node_content`.

The citation is the right kind of use for this built-in, and the commentary is not just an appeal to difficulty. I found no gap.
